passages.text: Then the high priest asked Stephen, “Are these charges true?”
passages.sermon: The high priest spoke to Stephen.\r\nThe high priest asked a question.\r\nHe said, “Are these charges true?”
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ ἀρχιερεύς Εἰ ταῦτα οὕτως ἔχει

passages.text: And Stephen declared: “Brothers and fathers, listen to me! The God of glory appeared to our father Abraham while he was still in Mesopotamia, before he lived in Haran, and told him, ‘Leave your country and your kindred and go to the land I will show you.’
passages.sermon:
Stephen spoke to the Sanhedrin.
He said, “Brothers and fathers, listen to me.
The God of glory appeared to our father Abraham.
God appeared to Abraham while he was still in Mesopotamia.
This was before Abraham lived in Haran.
God said to Abraham, ‘Leave your country.
Leave your relatives.
Go to the land I will show you.’”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἔφη Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοὶ καὶ πατέρες ἀκούσατε Ὁ Θεὸς τῆς δόξης ὤφθη τῷ πατρὶ ἡμῶν Ἀβραὰμ ὄντι ἐν τῇ Μεσοποταμίᾳ πρὶν ἢ κατοικῆσαι αὐτὸν ἐν Χαρράν καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν Ἔξελθε ἐκ τῆς γῆς σου καὶ ἐκ τῆς συγγενείας σου καὶ δεῦρο εἰς τὴν γῆν ἣν ἄν σοι δείξω

passages.text: So Abraham left the land of the Chaldeans and settled in Haran. After his father died, God brought him out of that place and into this land where you are now living.
passages.sermon:
Abraham was the father of the Jewish people.
Abraham lived in the land of the Chaldeans.
Abraham left the land of the Chaldeans.
Abraham settled in Haran.
Abraham’s father died in Haran.
God brought Abraham out of Haran.
God led Abraham into this land.
You now live in this land.
passages.original: τότε ἐξελθὼν ἐκ γῆς Χαλδαίων κατῴκησεν ἐν Χαρράν κἀκεῖθεν μετὰ τὸ ἀποθανεῖν τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ μετῴκισεν αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν γῆν ταύτην εἰς ἣν ὑμεῖς νῦν κατοικεῖτε

passages.text: He gave him no inheritance here, not even a foot of ground. But God promised to give possession of the land to Abraham and his descendants, even though he did not yet have a child.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Abraham.
God did not give Abraham any inheritance in this land.
God did not give Abraham even a foot of ground here.
God promised to give this land to Abraham.
God also promised to give this land to Abraham’s descendants after him.
At that time, Abraham did not have a child.
passages.original: Καὶ οὐκ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ κληρονομίαν ἐν αὐτῇ οὐδὲ βῆμα ποδός καὶ ἐπηγγείλατο δοῦναι αὐτῷ εἰς κατάσχεσιν αὐτὴν καὶ τῷ σπέρματι αὐτοῦ μετ’ αὐτόν οὐκ ὄντος αὐτῷ τέκνου

passages.text: God told him that his descendants would be foreigners in a strange land, and that they would be enslaved and mistreated four hundred years.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Abraham.
God said Abraham’s descendants would live in a foreign land.
They would not belong there.
People in that land would make them slaves.
They would treat them badly.
This would last four hundred years.
passages.original: ἐλάλησεν δὲ οὕτως ὁ Θεὸς ὅτι ἔσται τὸ σπέρμα αὐτοῦ πάροικον ἐν γῇ ἀλλοτρίᾳ καὶ δουλώσουσιν αὐτὸ καὶ κακώσουσιν ἔτη τετρακόσια

passages.text: ‘But I will punish the nation that enslaves them,’ God said, ‘and afterward they will come forth and worship Me in this place.’
passages.sermon:
God spoke about Abraham’s descendants.
God said another nation would enslave them.
God said, “I will punish that nation.”
After this, Abraham’s descendants will leave that land.
They will come here.
They will worship Me in this place.
passages.original: Καὶ τὸ ἔθνος ᾧ ἐὰν δουλεύσουσιν κρινῶ ἐγώ ὁ Θεὸς εἶπεν Καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ἐξελεύσονται καὶ λατρεύσουσίν μοι ἐν τῷ τόπῳ τούτῳ

passages.text: Then God gave Abraham the covenant of circumcision, and Abraham became the father of Isaac and circumcised him on the eighth day. And Isaac became the father of Jacob, and Jacob of the twelve patriarchs.
passages.sermon:
God gave Abraham the covenant of circumcision.
Abraham became the father of Isaac.
Abraham circumcised Isaac on the eighth day.
Isaac became the father of Jacob.
Jacob became the father of the twelve patriarchs.
passages.original: Καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ διαθήκην περιτομῆς καὶ οὕτως ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰσαὰκ καὶ περιέτεμεν αὐτὸν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ ὀγδόῃ καὶ Ἰσαὰκ τὸν Ἰακώβ καὶ Ἰακὼβ τοὺς δώδεκα πατριάρχας

passages.text: Because the patriarchs were jealous of Joseph, they sold him as a slave into Egypt. But God was with him and rescued him from all his troubles. He granted Joseph favor and wisdom in the sight of Pharaoh king of Egypt, who appointed him ruler over Egypt and all his household.
passages.sermon:
The patriarchs were Joseph’s brothers.
They became jealous of Joseph.
They sold Joseph as a slave.
They sent him into Egypt.
God was with Joseph.
God rescued Joseph from all his troubles.
God gave Joseph favor before Pharaoh, the king of Egypt.
God gave Joseph wisdom before Pharaoh.
Pharaoh appointed Joseph as ruler over Egypt.
Pharaoh put Joseph in charge of his whole household.
passages.original: Καὶ οἱ πατριάρχαι ζηλώσαντες τὸν Ἰωσὴφ ἀπέδοντο εἰς Αἴγυπτον καὶ ἦν ὁ Θεὸς μετ’ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐξείλατο αὐτὸν ἐκ πασῶν τῶν θλίψεων αὐτοῦ καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ χάριν καὶ σοφίαν ἐναντίον Φαραὼ βασιλέως Αἰγύπτου καὶ κατέστησεν αὐτὸν ἡγούμενον ἐπ’ Αἴγυπτον καὶ ἐφ’ ὅλον τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Then famine and great suffering swept across Egypt and Canaan, and our fathers could not find food.
passages.sermon: A famine came over all Egypt and Canaan.\r\nGreat suffering followed.\r\nOur fathers could not find food.
passages.original: Ἦλθεν δὲ λιμὸς ἐφ’ ὅλην τὴν Αἴγυπτον καὶ Χανάαν καὶ θλῖψις μεγάλη καὶ οὐχ ηὕρισκον χορτάσματα οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν

passages.text: When Jacob heard that there was grain in Egypt, he sent our fathers on their first visit.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the father of the twelve patriarchs.
Jacob heard that there was grain in Egypt.
Jacob sent our fathers to Egypt.
This was their first visit.
passages.original: ἀκούσας δὲ Ἰακὼβ ὄντα σιτία εἰς Αἴγυπτον ἐξαπέστειλεν τοὺς πατέρας ἡμῶν πρῶτον

passages.text: On their second visit, Joseph revealed his identity to his brothers, and his family became known to Pharaoh.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was the son of Jacob.
Joseph had brothers.
Joseph lived in Egypt.
Joseph’s brothers visited Egypt.
This was their second visit.
Joseph revealed his identity to his brothers.
Pharaoh was the ruler of Egypt.
Pharaoh learned about Joseph’s family.
passages.original: καὶ ἐν τῷ δευτέρῳ ἀνεγνωρίσθη Ἰωσὴφ τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς αὐτοῦ καὶ φανερὸν ἐγένετο τῷ Φαραὼ τὸ γένος τοῦ Ἰωσήφ

passages.text: Then Joseph sent for his father Jacob and all his relatives, seventy-five in all.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was in Egypt.
Joseph sent a message to his father Jacob.
Joseph asked Jacob to come to Egypt.
Joseph also asked all his relatives to come.
There were seventy-five people in total.
passages.original: ἀποστείλας δὲ Ἰωσὴφ μετεκαλέσατο Ἰακὼβ τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ καὶ πᾶσαν τὴν συγγένειαν ἐν ψυχαῖς ἑβδομήκοντα πέντε

passages.text: So Jacob went down to Egypt, where he and our fathers died.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the father of Joseph.
Jacob went down to Egypt.
Jacob died in Egypt.
Our fathers died in Egypt.
passages.original: Καὶ κατέβη Ἰακὼβ εἰς Αἴγυπτον καὶ ἐτελεύτησεν αὐτὸς καὶ οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν

passages.text: Their bones were carried back to Shechem and placed in the tomb that Abraham had bought from the sons of Hamor at Shechem for a price he paid in silver.
passages.sermon:
Abraham was the ancestor of Jacob and Joseph.
Abraham bought a tomb in Shechem.
He paid the sons of Hamor in Shechem with silver for the tomb.
After Jacob and our fathers died, people carried their bones to Shechem.
They placed the bones in the tomb Abraham had bought.
passages.original: καὶ μετετέθησαν εἰς Συχὲμ καὶ ἐτέθησαν ἐν τῷ μνήματι ᾧ ὠνήσατο Ἀβραὰμ τιμῆς ἀργυρίου παρὰ τῶν υἱῶν Ἑμμὼρ ἐν Συχέμ

passages.text: As the time drew near for God to fulfill His promise to Abraham, our people in Egypt increased greatly in number.
passages.sermon:
God made a promise to Abraham.
The time for God to fulfill this promise came closer.
Our people lived in Egypt.
Our people grew in number.
Our people became very many in Egypt.
passages.original: Καθὼς δὲ ἤγγιζεν ὁ χρόνος τῆς ἐπαγγελίας ἧς ὡμολόγησεν ὁ Θεὸς τῷ Ἀβραάμ ηὔξησεν ὁ λαὸς καὶ ἐπληθύνθη ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ

passages.text: Then another king, who knew nothing of Joseph, arose over Egypt.
passages.sermon: A new king began to rule over Egypt.\r\nThis king did not know Joseph.
passages.original: ἄχρι οὗ ἀνέστη βασιλεὺς ἕτερος ἐπ’ Αἴγυπτον ὃς οὐκ ᾔδει τὸν Ἰωσήφ

passages.text: He exploited our people and oppressed our fathers, forcing them to abandon their infants so they would die.
passages.sermon:
A new king ruled over Egypt.
This king did not know Joseph.
He acted with cunning against our people.
He oppressed our fathers.
He forced our fathers to abandon their babies.
He wanted the babies to die.
passages.original: οὗτος κατασοφισάμενος τὸ γένος ἡμῶν ἐκάκωσεν τοὺς πατέρας ἡμῶν τοῦ ποιεῖν τὰ βρέφη ἔκθετα αὐτῶν εἰς τὸ μὴ ζωογονεῖσθαι

passages.text: At that time Moses was born, and he was beautiful in the sight of God. For three months he was nurtured in his father’s house.
passages.sermon:
Moses was born at that time.
God saw Moses as beautiful.
Moses lived in his father’s house for three months.
His family cared for him during those three months.
passages.original: Ἐν ᾧ καιρῷ ἐγεννήθη Μωϋσῆς καὶ ἦν ἀστεῖος τῷ Θεῷ ὃς ἀνετράφη μῆνας τρεῖς ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ τοῦ πατρός

passages.text: When he was set outside, Pharaoh’s daughter took him and brought him up as her own son.
passages.sermon: Pharaoh’s daughter found Moses after someone set him outside.\r\nShe took Moses.\r\nShe raised Moses as her own son.
passages.original: ἐκτεθέντος δὲ αὐτοῦ ἀνείλατο αὐτὸν ἡ θυγάτηρ Φαραὼ καὶ ἀνεθρέψατο αὐτὸν ἑαυτῇ εἰς υἱόν

passages.text: So Moses was educated in all the wisdom of the Egyptians and was powerful in speech and action.
passages.sermon:
Moses was a Hebrew man.
He grew up in Egypt.
He learned all the wisdom of the Egyptians.
He became powerful in his words.
He became powerful in his actions.
passages.original: καὶ ἐπαιδεύθη Μωϋσῆς ἐν πάσῃ σοφίᾳ Αἰγυπτίων ἦν δὲ δυνατὸς ἐν λόγοις καὶ ἔργοις αὐτοῦ

passages.text: When Moses was forty years old, he decided to visit his brothers, the children of Israel.
passages.sermon:
Moses was a Hebrew man.
Pharaoh’s daughter raised Moses as her own son in Egypt.
Moses learned all the wisdom of the Egyptians.
Moses became powerful in speech and action.
When Moses reached forty years old, he made a decision.
He decided to visit his brothers.
His brothers were the children of Israel.
passages.original: Ὡς δὲ ἐπληροῦτο αὐτῷ τεσσερακονταέτης χρόνος ἀνέβη ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν αὐτοῦ ἐπισκέψασθαι τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς αὐτοῦ τοὺς υἱοὺς Ἰσραήλ

passages.text: And when he saw one of them being mistreated, Moses went to his defense and avenged him by striking down the Egyptian who was oppressing him.
passages.sermon:
Moses saw one of his fellow Israelites being mistreated.
Moses defended the man who was suffering.
Moses avenged the oppressed Israelite.
Moses struck down the Egyptian who was oppressing him.
passages.original: καὶ ἰδών τινα ἀδικούμενον ἠμύνατο καὶ ἐποίησεν ἐκδίκησιν τῷ καταπονουμένῳ πατάξας τὸν Αἰγύπτιον

passages.text: He assumed his brothers would understand that God was using him to deliver them, but they did not.
passages.sermon:
Moses was forty years old.
Moses visited his brothers, the Israelites.
Moses believed something about his brothers.
He believed his brothers would understand him.
Moses thought God was working through him.
He thought God was giving salvation to the Israelites by his hand.
But his brothers did not understand this.
passages.original: ἐνόμιζεν δὲ συνιέναι τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς αὐτοῦ ὅτι ὁ Θεὸς διὰ χειρὸς αὐτοῦ δίδωσιν σωτηρίαν αὐτοῖς οἱ δὲ οὐ συνῆκαν

passages.text: The next day he came upon two Israelites who were fighting, and he tried to reconcile them, saying, ‘Men, you are brothers. Why are you mistreating each other?’
passages.sermon:
Moses was an Israelite.
The next day, Moses saw two Israelites fighting.
Moses tried to make peace between them.
He spoke to them.
He said, "Men, you are brothers."
He asked, "Why are you mistreating each other?"
passages.original: Τῇ τε ἐπιούσῃ ἡμέρᾳ ὤφθη αὐτοῖς μαχομένοις καὶ συνήλλασσεν αὐτοὺς εἰς εἰρήνην εἰπών Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί ἐστε ἱνα‿ τί ἀδικεῖτε ἀλλήλους

passages.text: But the man who was abusing his neighbor pushed Moses aside and said, ‘Who made you ruler and judge over us?
passages.sermon:
A man was hurting his neighbor.
This man pushed Moses away.
He spoke to Moses.
He said, "Who made you ruler over us?"
He said, "Who made you judge over us?"
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἀδικῶν τὸν πλησίον ἀπώσατο αὐτὸν εἰπών Τίς σε κατέστησεν ἄρχοντα καὶ δικαστὴν ἐφ’ ἡμῶν

passages.text: Do you want to kill me as you killed the Egyptian yesterday?’
passages.sermon:
The man spoke to Moses.
He asked Moses a question.
He said, "Do you want to kill me?"
He reminded Moses of a past event.
He said, "You killed the Egyptian yesterday."
He compared his situation to the Egyptian's.
He asked if Moses wanted to kill him in the same way.
passages.original: μὴ ἀνελεῖν με σὺ θέλεις ὃν τρόπον ἀνεῖλες ἐχθὲς τὸν Αἰγύπτιον

passages.text: At this remark, Moses fled to the land of Midian, where he lived as a foreigner and had two sons.
passages.sermon:
Moses heard the man’s words.
Moses fled because of what the man said.
Moses went to the land of Midian.
Moses lived there as a foreigner.
Moses had two sons in Midian.
passages.original: ἔφυγεν δὲ Μωϋσῆς ἐν τῷ λόγῳ τούτῳ καὶ ἐγένετο πάροικος ἐν γῇ Μαδιάμ οὗ ἐγέννησεν υἱοὺς δύο

passages.text: After forty years had passed, an angel appeared to Moses in the flames of a burning bush in the desert near Mount Sinai.
passages.sermon:
Moses was living in the desert near Mount Sinai.
Forty years passed.
An angel appeared to Moses.
The angel appeared in flames of fire.
The flames were in a bush.
passages.original: Καὶ πληρωθέντων ἐτῶν τεσσεράκοντα ὤφθη αὐτῷ ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ τοῦ ὄρους Σινᾶ ἄγγελος ἐν φλογὶ πυρὸς βάτου

passages.text: When Moses saw it, he marveled at the sight. As he approached to look more closely, the voice of the Lord came to him: ‘I am the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.’ Moses trembled with fear and did not dare to look.
passages.sermon:
Moses was a Hebrew man.
He saw a strange sight in the desert near Mount Sinai.
He saw a bush that burned with fire but was not consumed.
Moses marveled at this vision.
He went closer to look at the bush.
As Moses approached, he heard the voice of the Lord.
The Lord spoke to Moses.
The Lord said, “I am the God of your fathers.”
The Lord said, “I am the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.”
Moses became afraid.
Moses trembled with fear.
Moses did not dare to look at the bush.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ Μωϋσῆς ἰδὼν ἐθαύμαζεν τὸ ὅραμα προσερχομένου δὲ αὐτοῦ κατανοῆσαι ἐγένετο φωνὴ Κυρίου Ἐγὼ ὁ Θεὸς τῶν πατέρων σου ὁ Θεὸς Ἀβραὰμ καὶ Ἰσαὰκ καὶ Ἰακώβ ἔντρομος δὲ γενόμενος Μωϋσῆς οὐκ ἐτόλμα κατανοῆσαι

passages.text: Then the Lord said to him, ‘Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy ground.
passages.sermon:
The Lord spoke to Moses.
The Lord said, "Take off your sandals."
The ground where you are standing is holy."
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ Κύριος Λῦσον τὸ ὑπόδημα τῶν ποδῶν σου ὁ γὰρ τόπος ἐφ’ ᾧ ἕστηκας γῆ ἁγία ἐστίν

passages.text: I have indeed seen the oppression of My people in Egypt. I have heard their groaning and have come down to deliver them. Now come, I will send you back to Egypt.’
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Moses.
God said, “I have seen the suffering of My people in Egypt.
I have heard their groaning.
I have come down to rescue them.
Now, come.
I will send you to Egypt.”
passages.original: ἰδὼν εἶδον τὴν κάκωσιν τοῦ λαοῦ μου τοῦ ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ καὶ τοῦ στεναγμοῦ αὐτοῦ ἤκουσα καὶ κατέβην ἐξελέσθαι αὐτούς καὶ νῦν δεῦρο ἀποστείλω σε εἰς Αἴγυπτον

passages.text: This Moses, whom they had rejected with the words, ‘Who made you ruler and judge?’ is the one whom God sent to be their ruler and redeemer through the angel who appeared to him in the bush.
passages.sermon:
Moses was a leader of the Israelites.
The Israelites had rejected Moses.
They said to him, "Who made you ruler and judge?"
God chose Moses.
God sent Moses to be their ruler.
God sent Moses to be their redeemer.
God sent Moses through the angel.
The angel appeared to Moses in the bush.
passages.original: Τοῦτον τὸν Μωϋσῆν ὃν ἠρνήσαντο εἰπόντες Τίς σε κατέστησεν ἄρχοντα καὶ δικαστήν τοῦτον ὁ Θεὸς καὶ ἄρχοντα καὶ λυτρωτὴν ἀπέσταλκεν σὺν χειρὶ ἀγγέλου τοῦ ὀφθέντος αὐτῷ ἐν τῇ βάτῳ

passages.text: He led them out and performed wonders and signs in the land of Egypt, at the Red Sea, and for forty years in the wilderness.
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of the Israelites.
He led the Israelites out of Egypt.
He performed wonders and signs in Egypt.
He performed wonders and signs at the Red Sea.
He performed wonders and signs in the wilderness for forty years.
passages.original: οὗτος ἐξήγαγεν αὐτοὺς ποιήσας τέρατα καὶ σημεῖα ἐν γῇ Αἰγύπτῳ καὶ ἐν Ἐρυθρᾷ Θαλάσσῃ καὶ ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ ἔτη τεσσεράκοντα

passages.text: This is the same Moses who told the Israelites, ‘God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your brothers.’
passages.sermon:
Moses was a leader of Israel.
Moses spoke to the Israelites.
Moses said, “God will raise up a prophet for you.”
This prophet will be like me.
God will choose him from among your own brothers.
passages.original: Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ Μωϋσῆς ὁ εἴπας τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἰσραήλ Προφήτην ὑμῖν ἀναστήσει ὁ Θεὸς ἐκ τῶν ἀδελφῶν ὑμῶν ὡς ἐμέ

passages.text: He was in the assembly in the wilderness with the angel who spoke to him on Mount Sinai, and with our fathers. And he received living words to pass on to us.
passages.sermon:
Moses was with the people of Israel in the wilderness.
He was with the angel who spoke to him on Mount Sinai.
He was also with our ancestors.
Moses received living words from God.
He received these words to give them to us.
passages.original: οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ γενόμενος ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ μετὰ τοῦ ἀγγέλου τοῦ λαλοῦντος αὐτῷ ἐν τῷ ὄρει Σινᾶ καὶ τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν ὃς ἐδέξατο λόγια ζῶντα δοῦναι ἡμῖν

passages.text: But our fathers refused to obey him. Instead, they rejected him and in their hearts turned back to Egypt.
passages.sermon:
Moses led the Israelites.
Our fathers did not want to obey Moses.
They rejected Moses.
In their hearts, they turned back to Egypt.
passages.original: ᾧ οὐκ ἠθέλησαν ὑπήκοοι γενέσθαι οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν ἀλλὰ ἀπώσαντο καὶ ἐστράφησαν ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις αὐτῶν εἰς Αἴγυπτον

passages.text: They said to Aaron, ‘Make us gods who will go before us! As for this Moses who led us out of the land of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him.’
passages.sermon:
The Israelites spoke to Aaron.
They said, "Make us gods who will go before us."
Moses led us out of the land of Egypt.
We do not know what has happened to Moses.
passages.original: εἰπόντες τῷ Ἀαρών Ποίησον ἡμῖν θεοὺς οἳ προπορεύσονται ἡμῶν ὁ γὰρ Μωϋσῆς οὗτος ὃς ἐξήγαγεν ἡμᾶς ἐκ γῆς Αἰγύπτου οὐκ οἴδαμεν τί ἐγένετο αὐτῷ

passages.text: At that time they made a calf and offered a sacrifice to the idol, rejoicing in the works of their hands.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites lived in the wilderness during those days.
They made a calf from their own hands.
They offered a sacrifice to this idol.
They rejoiced in what they had made themselves.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐμοσχοποίησαν ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις καὶ ἀνήγαγον θυσίαν τῷ εἰδώλῳ καὶ εὐφραίνοντο ἐν τοῖς ἔργοις τῶν χειρῶν αὐτῶν

passages.text: But God turned away from them and gave them over to the worship of the host of heaven, as it is written in the book of the prophets: ‘Did you bring Me sacrifices and offerings forty years in the wilderness, O house of Israel?
passages.sermon:
God turned away from the people of Israel.
God let them worship the host of heaven.
The host of heaven means the sun, moon, and stars.
This is written in the book of the prophets.
God said to the house of Israel,
“Did you bring Me sacrifices and offerings for forty years in the wilderness?”
passages.original: ἔστρεψεν δὲ ὁ Θεὸς καὶ παρέδωκεν αὐτοὺς λατρεύειν τῇ στρατιᾷ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καθὼς γέγραπται ἐν βίβλῳ τῶν προφητῶν Μὴ σφάγια καὶ θυσίας προσηνέγκατέ μοι ἔτη τεσσεράκοντα ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ οἶκος Ἰσραήλ

passages.text: You have taken along the tabernacle of Molech and the star of your god Rephan, the idols you made to worship. Therefore I will send you into exile beyond Babylon.’
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel took the tabernacle of Molech.
They also took the star of their god Rephan.
These were idols.
The people made these idols to worship them.
God said He would send the people into exile.
God said this exile would be beyond Babylon.
passages.original: καὶ ἀνελάβετε τὴν σκηνὴν τοῦ Μολὸχ καὶ τὸ ἄστρον τοῦ θεοῦ ὑμῶν Ῥαιφάν τοὺς τύπους οὓς ἐποιήσατε προσκυνεῖν αὐτοῖς καὶ μετοικιῶ ὑμᾶς ἐπέκεινα Βαβυλῶνος

passages.text: Our fathers had the tabernacle of the Testimony with them in the wilderness. It was constructed exactly as God had directed Moses, according to the pattern he had seen.
passages.sermon:
Our fathers were the people of Israel.
They traveled in the wilderness.
They had the tabernacle of the Testimony with them.
God spoke to Moses.
God told Moses how to build the tabernacle.
God showed Moses a pattern for the tabernacle.
Moses made the tabernacle exactly as God commanded.
The tabernacle matched the pattern God showed Moses.
passages.original: Ἡ σκηνὴ τοῦ μαρτυρίου ἦν τοῖς πατράσιν ἡμῶν ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ καθὼς διετάξατο ὁ λαλῶν τῷ Μωϋσῇ ποιῆσαι αὐτὴν κατὰ τὸν τύπον ὃν ἑωράκει

passages.text: And our fathers who received it brought it in with Joshua when they dispossessed the nations God drove out before them. It remained until the time of David, who found favor in the sight of God and asked to provide a dwelling place for the God of Jacob.
passages.sermon:
Our fathers received the tabernacle of the Testimony from God.
They brought the tabernacle into the land with Joshua.
Joshua led them as they entered the land.
God drove out the nations before our fathers.
The tabernacle remained with them until the time of David.
David found favor in the sight of God.
David asked to provide a dwelling place for the God of Jacob.
passages.original: ἣν καὶ εἰσήγαγον διαδεξάμενοι οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν μετὰ Ἰησοῦ ἐν τῇ κατασχέσει τῶν ἐθνῶν ὧν ἐξῶσεν ὁ Θεὸς ἀπὸ προσώπου τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν ἕως τῶν ἡμερῶν Δαυίδ ὃς εὗρεν χάριν ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ ᾐτήσατο εὑρεῖν σκήνωμα τῷ Θεῷ Ἰακώβ

passages.text: But it was Solomon who built the house for Him.
passages.sermon:
Solomon was a king of Israel.
Solomon built a house for God.
Solomon completed this house.
This house was for the God of Israel.
passages.original: Σολομῶν δὲ οἰκοδόμησεν αὐτῷ οἶκον

passages.text: However, the Most High does not dwell in houses made by human hands. As the prophet says: ‘Heaven is My throne and the earth is My footstool. What kind of house will you build for Me, says the Lord, or where will My place of repose be?
passages.sermon:
The Most High is God.
God does not live in houses made by human hands.
A prophet spoke God's words.
God said, "Heaven is My throne."
God said, "The earth is My footstool."
God asked, "What kind of house will you build for Me?"
God asked, "Where will My resting place be?"
passages.original: Ἀλλ’ οὐχ ὁ Ὕψιστος ἐν χειροποιήτοις κατοικεῖ καθὼς ὁ προφήτης λέγει Ὁ οὐρανός μοι θρόνος ἡ δὲ γῆ ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν μου ποῖον οἶκον οἰκοδομήσετέ μοι λέγει Κύριος ἢ τίς τόπος τῆς καταπαύσεώς μου

passages.text: Has not My hand made all these things?’
passages.sermon: God speaks.\r\nGod says, “I made all these things with My own hand.”\r\nGod created everything.
passages.original: οὐχὶ ἡ χείρ μου ἐποίησεν ταῦτα πάντα

passages.text: You stiff-necked people with uncircumcised hearts and ears! You always resist the Holy Spirit, just as your fathers did.
passages.sermon:
Stephen spoke to the Jewish leaders.
He called them stiff-necked people.
He said their hearts were hard.
He said their ears were closed.
He told them they always resisted the Holy Spirit.
He said their fathers also resisted the Holy Spirit.
He said they acted just like their fathers.
passages.original: Σκληροτράχηλοι καὶ ἀπερίτμητοι καρδίαις καὶ τοῖς ὠσίν ὑμεῖς ἀεὶ τῷ Πνεύματι τῷ Ἁγίῳ ἀντιπίπτετε ὡς οἱ πατέρες ὑμῶν καὶ ὑμεῖς

passages.text: Which of the prophets did your fathers fail to persecute? They even killed those who foretold the coming of the Righteous One. And now you are His betrayers and murderers— you who received the law ordained by angels, yet have not kept it.”
passages.sermon:
Stephen spoke to the Jewish leaders.
He said their ancestors persecuted every prophet.
Their ancestors killed those who announced the coming of the Righteous One.
The Righteous One is Jesus.
Now these leaders have betrayed and murdered Jesus.
They received the law given through angels.
They have not obeyed that law.
passages.original: τίνα τῶν προφητῶν οὐκ ἐδίωξαν οἱ πατέρες ὑμῶν καὶ ἀπέκτειναν τοὺς προκαταγγείλαντας περὶ τῆς ἐλεύσεως τοῦ Δικαίου οὗ νῦν ὑμεῖς προδόται καὶ φονεῖς ἐγένεσθε οἵτινες ἐλάβετε τὸν νόμον εἰς διαταγὰς ἀγγέλων καὶ οὐκ ἐφυλάξατε

passages.text: On hearing this, the members of the Sanhedrin were enraged, and they gnashed their teeth at him.
passages.sermon:
The members of the Sanhedrin heard these words.
They became very angry.
They felt deep rage in their hearts.
They gnashed their teeth at Stephen.
passages.original: Ἀκούοντες δὲ ταῦτα διεπρίοντο ταῖς καρδίαις αὐτῶν καὶ ἔβρυχον τοὺς ὀδόντας ἐπ’ αὐτόν

passages.text: But Stephen, full of the Holy Spirit, looked intently into heaven and saw the glory of God and Jesus standing at the right hand of God.
passages.sermon:
Stephen was full of the Holy Spirit.
Stephen looked up into heaven.
Stephen saw the glory of God.
Stephen saw Jesus.
Jesus was standing at the right hand of God.
passages.original: ὑπάρχων δὲ πλήρης Πνεύματος Ἁγίου ἀτενίσας εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν εἶδεν δόξαν Θεοῦ καὶ Ἰησοῦν ἑστῶτα ἐκ δεξιῶν τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: “Look,” he said, “I see heaven open and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God.”
passages.sermon:
Stephen was full of the Holy Spirit.
He looked up into heaven.
He saw the glory of God.
He saw Jesus standing at the right hand of God.
Stephen said, “Look, I see heaven open.
I see the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God.”
passages.original: καὶ εἶπεν Ἰδοὺ θεωρῶ τοὺς οὐρανοὺς διηνοιγμένους καὶ τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκ δεξιῶν ἑστῶτα τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: At this they covered their ears, cried out in a loud voice, and rushed together at him.
passages.sermon:
The people heard Stephen speak.
They cried out with a loud voice.
They covered their ears.
They all rushed at Stephen together.
passages.original: Κράξαντες δὲ φωνῇ μεγάλῃ συνέσχον τὰ ὦτα αὐτῶν καὶ ὥρμησαν ὁμοθυμαδὸν ἐπ’ αὐτόν

passages.text: They dragged him out of the city and began to stone him. Meanwhile the witnesses laid their garments at the feet of a young man named Saul.
passages.sermon:
The crowd dragged Stephen out of the city.
They began to stone Stephen.
The witnesses took off their garments.
They laid their garments at the feet of a young man.
The young man was named Saul.
passages.original: καὶ ἐκβαλόντες ἔξω τῆς πόλεως ἐλιθοβόλουν καὶ οἱ μάρτυρες ἀπέθεντο τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτῶν παρὰ τοὺς πόδας νεανίου καλουμένου Σαύλου

passages.text: While they were stoning him, Stephen appealed, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.”
passages.sermon:
Stephen was a follower of Jesus.
\r\nPeople threw stones at Stephen.
\r\nStephen called out to Jesus.
\r\nStephen said, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἐλιθοβόλουν τὸν Στέφανον ἐπικαλούμενον καὶ λέγοντα Κύριε Ἰησοῦ δέξαι τὸ πνεῦμά μου

passages.text: Falling on his knees, he cried out in a loud voice, “Lord, do not hold this sin against them.” And when he had said this, he fell asleep.
passages.sermon:
Stephen was a follower of Jesus.
People were stoning Stephen.
Stephen fell to his knees.
Stephen cried out in a loud voice.
Stephen said, “Lord, do not hold this sin against them.”
After Stephen said this, he died.
passages.original: θεὶς δὲ τὰ γόνατα ἔκραξεν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ Κύριε μὴ στήσῃς αὐτοῖς ταύτην τὴν ἁμαρτίαν καὶ τοῦτο εἰπὼν ἐκοιμήθη
